subject: science
passage: New Caledonian crows, found on islands in the South Pacific, are famous for making tools: they shape twigs and strips of leaf into hooks and probes that pull insects out of holes in wood. Young crows stay with their parents for up to two years, and ornithologist Mele Taufa argues that this long period of watching adults is how the birds learn to make and use tools.
passage_b: In one study, young New Caledonian crows were raised by people, with no adult crows to watch. Within a few months, the birds began poking sticks into crevices on their own. Their early tools were simple and clumsy compared with those of wild adults. The researchers concluded that the basic urge to use tools is inborn, though experience and observation may help the birds refine their skills.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the argument in Text 1?

choices.A: By agreeing that young crows cannot use tools until they have watched adults
choices.B: By suggesting that watching adults may refine tool use but is not where it begins
choices.C: By arguing that young crows learn tool use mainly from crows other than their parents
choices.D: By claiming that observation plays no part in how crows develop tool skills

explanation.why: Taufa argues in Text 1 that young crows learn tool use by watching adults. In Text 2, crows with "no adult crows to watch" still began using sticks, so the basic urge is "inborn," though "observation may help the birds refine their skills." Text 2 would say watching adults explains the refinement of tool use, not its origin.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The crows in Text 2 used sticks "on their own" with no adults to watch, the opposite of this choice.
explanation.B: Correct. Text 2 says the basic urge is inborn, while observation may help refine skills.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 never compares learning from parents with learning from other crows.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 says observation "may help the birds refine their skills," so it does not rule observation out.
